note: Curated public copy only. This file deliberately contains no repository paths: config/repository-layout.yaml is authoritative for where files live, and a path duplicated here would be a second place that can drift. Modules are named by logical key; Phase 2 binds each key to a layout-contract component identifier. Everything derivable from the ontology - class counts, definition coverage, category distribution - is generated at build time and must not appear here.

site.name: BFO-Aligned ValueNet
site.tagline: An ontology of human values as realizable entities
site.summary: ValueNet represents a value not as a label attached to a thing, but as a realizable entity that inheres in an agent and is realized in the processes where that agent appraises, chooses, feels, or acts.
site.base_path_note: The site is served from a project subpath. Every internal URL is relative; none may assume the site is at the domain root.

iri_resolution.text: Canonical ValueNet IRIs identify ontology entities but are not currently HTTP-dereferenceable. Use the explorer, repository source links, or module downloads to inspect their definitions.
iri_resolution.why: The canonical namespace does not resolve today. An IRI rendered as a link would send a reader to a 404 and imply the ontology is broken. IRIs stay copyable and searchable and are never presented as fetchable URLs.

reserved_aliases.text: The w3id.org ValueNet IRIs that appear as rdfs:seeAlso are reserved aliases. They are not registered, nothing is declared under them, and no query should rely on them.
reserved_aliases.why: Stated in the core module's own namespace policy; repeated publicly so a reader does not treat an alias as an alternative endpoint.

build_label.why: A Pages build is not a release. The full source commit is displayed alongside this label, and the word release is reserved for a signed-off tag.

license_pending.text: No project license has been issued yet. No reuse terms are granted for ValueNet-authored material, and terms must not be inferred from vendored BFO or CCO files, which carry their own upstream licenses.
license_pending.why: Placeholder until the publication plan's Phase 0 governance gate completes. This notice is removed, not edited, when LICENSE, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, and CITATION.cff exist.

product_hierarchy.label: BFO-Aligned ValueNet
product_hierarchy.role: The maintained, primary public ontology suite.

product_hierarchy.label: Original ValueNet
product_hierarchy.role: The DUL-aligned source tradition, lexical trigger data, and empirical corpora. The mapping target, not a deprecated release.

product_hierarchy.label: MAREP
product_hierarchy.role: The audit framework that produces the quality evidence. Evidence about the work, not a prerequisite for using the ontology.

value_proposition.heading: A bearer
value_proposition.body: A value disposition inheres in an agent. Asking whose value it is has an answer in the model rather than in a naming convention.

value_proposition.heading: A realization
value_proposition.body: Holding a value and acting on it are different entities. The disposition persists; the value realization process occurs. So does its counterpart, the violation process, which lets the suite say an act contravened a value without asserting the agent lacks it.

value_proposition.heading: Interoperability by construction
value_proposition.body: Every class descends from a BFO or CCO term, so ValueNet composes with other BFO-aligned ontologies instead of needing a bespoke bridge to each one.

modules.purpose: Top-level entities: the disposition and role split, realization and violation processes, and the textual-evidence chain. Every other module imports this.
Schwartz's ten Basic Human Values as BFO dispositions, serving as the high-level classification for finer-grained terms.
The folk-value vocabulary, the large and specific layer people actually name in text, classified under the Schwartz values.
modules.note: This module declares no dcterms:title or dcterms:description. Its display name and purpose here are curated, not extracted, and are marked as such wherever the site distinguishes generated from authored copy.

modules.purpose: Haidt's Moral Foundations as BFO dispositions, with the violation processes that contravene them.
The cognitive acts by which agents assess one another morally: behavioural observation, prudent discernment, and rash judgment.
Annotation-only correspondences from BFO-aligned terms to the original ValueNet and related value ontologies.
modules.note: Declares no classes. It contributes mapping annotations to classes defined elsewhere, so it appears in the module catalog and downloads but produces no class records.

modules.purpose: Supplies the definition ValueCore omits for the vcvf:triggers property. Annotation only; it adds no logical axiom.
modules.note: Declares zero classes by design. The module card displays zero as a measured property, not as a discovery failure. This module also declares no dcterms:title; its display name is curated.

vendored.label: Upstream dependencies
vendored.body: BFO core and a pinned Common Core Ontologies extract are included so the suite can be loaded offline. They are upstream material under their own licenses, are never presented as ValueNet-authored modules, and are excluded from the authored class catalog and the default download bundle.

mapping_policy.body: Correspondences to the original ValueNet are recorded with ValueNet annotation properties and are published exactly as asserted. They are not SKOS mapping relations and are never translated into any.
mapping_policy.why: Asserting historical or conceptual correspondence is a weaker and more honest claim than logical equivalence, and rewriting the predicate would silently strengthen it.

evidence_statement.body: Ontology changes here are measured rather than asserted. The repository records a semantic fingerprint of the whole corpus that reproduces from any checkout, an experiment showing why earlier digests did not, and a triple-by-triple record of every source-data repair made since.
evidence_statement.tone: State what is measured and link to it. Do not characterise the ontology as verified, validated, or correct; those are claims the evidence does not make.
